commercialPostureNote: Lane D produces candidate evidence. This packet opens no checkout, no sponsorship, no packet credit and no commercial status. Only COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN authorizes any of those, and this route is INCOMPLETE and stays INCOMPLETE after this lane's patch request.

pageByPage.covers: How to file; matter identification with the ground named; what is in the packet; the order operations are done in; where to file; filing fee.
pageByPage.findings: The ground is named on the first line a participant reads, so a misdemeanor petitioner is never shown a felony clean period. Service-before-filing is step 1 and is stated before the filing step, matching N.D.C.C. 12-60.1-03(4). The prosecuting attorney and the service method are the participant's own governed facts, not a placeholder. No fee amount appears; the fee paragraph says to ask the clerk and to ask about proceeding without payment of fees.

pageByPage.covers: Copies; after you file; the five stop conditions.
pageByPage.findings: The 45-day hearing floor, the clear-and-convincing burden and the up-to-one-year refiling bar all appear before the participant files rather than after. All five stop conditions are present and each says what to do, not merely that a risk exists. Stop condition 5 routes an impaired-driving record to N.D.C.C. 39-08-01.6 instead of leaving the participant with a denial.

pageByPage.covers: What sealing does and does not reach; safety statement; footer.
pageByPage.findings: The court-and-prosecution-records-only limit is stated to the participant before filing, so the packet cannot be read as promising a clean background check. Safety statement and the not-an-official-form footer both present.

pageByPage.covers: Caption; docket and judicial district; document title; statutory authority; I. Jurisdiction and venue; II. Parties.
pageByPage.findings: Criminal caption with the State as Plaintiff and the filer as Petitioner, the correct shape for a petition filed in the existing criminal case. Three authority rows, each a statute with text carried verbatim from the state pack; the filing-instruction row that read as authority in the first draft is gone. Aliases are alleged, which ndFilingInstructions[4] requires. No other state's sovereign, court or agency appears.

pageByPage.covers: III. Facts and case history, paragraphs 6 to 10; IV. Eligibility allegations, paragraphs 11 to 20.
pageByPage.findings: Charge, arresting agency, conviction date, offence grade and the N.D.C.C. section are each alleged separately rather than compressed. Every content item ndFilingInstructions[4] requires is alleged: address history at paragraph 18, complete criminal history across North Dakota, other states, federal court and foreign countries, all prior and pending charges including deferred and continued-for-dismissal matters, prior relief requests in any forum, rehabilitation, and the reasons sealing is asked for. The 12-60.1-04(1)(c) and (d) findings are alleged as facts with dates. Allegations are numbered continuously from the previous page with no repeat and no gap. Nothing is asserted by LegalEase; every narrative value is the participant's.

pageByPage.covers: V. Requested relief; VI. Verification; signature block; date-of-birth note; filed-with list; footer.
pageByPage.findings: Relief clause (a) asks for the exact findings 12-60.1-04(1) requires and clause (b) asks for sealing of court and prosecution records only. The default agency-wide clause is absent and asserted absent by test. Section numerals are unique — the duplicate V. the first draft produced is gone, and the address history is now a numbered allegation in section IV where it belongs. Signature rule, signer, address and date line are whole on one page. No penalty recital, because no committed source ties a verification statute to this petition.

pageByPage.covers: Order caption; docket; [PROPOSED] ORDER; AND NOW recital; three operative paragraphs; BY THE COURT block; footer.
pageByPage.findings: The order seals court and prosecution records, states what sealing prohibits, and states what it does not reach. The judge's signature block is blank for the court and whole on the page. The petition's in-document heading is suppressed because this is a standalone document.

pageByPage.covers: Proof of service heading; the rule service was made under; certification; recipient and address field; service method field; signature and date block; footer.
pageByPage.findings: The document states the rule it is filed under (12-60.1-03(4), N.D.R.Crim.P. 49, N.D.R.Civ.P. 5(b)) rather than instructing the participant, which is the right register for a document filed with the court. Prosecutor address and service method remain confirm-before-filing fields rather than a guessed address. Signature block whole on the page.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The petition carried two sections numbered V — REQUESTED RELIEF and a composer-added ADDRESS HISTORY — and the address history appeared after the signature block, so a required content item sat outside the signed body.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: Address history became a numbered allegation inside section IV, ahead of the requested relief and the signature. The duplicate numeral is gone and a test asserts the petition's section numerals are unique.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The statutory-authority block carried a row citing N.D.C.C. 12-60.1-03 whose text was a participant filing instruction ('Prepare at minimum a Petition...'), which is the wrong register for a court filing's authority block.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: Removed from primaryStatutoryAuthority. The filing requirement stays in the participant guide, where it is an instruction rather than an authority.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The proof of service opened with the prosecutor's own canvassing duty under 12-60.1-04(4), which is context for the participant rather than a statement belonging on a document filed with the court.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: The service note now states the rule the service was made under. The canvassing duty stays in the participant guide and in stop condition 2.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The eligibility allegations stated the clean-period rule twice: once as the renderer's waiting-period text and once as the petitioner's own allegation.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: The rule is stated once, in the statutory-authority block; the allegation states the fact.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The participant guide stated the 45-day hearing floor twice in adjacent paragraphs under AFTER YOU FILE, and stated the sealing scope twice in adjacent paragraphs.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: One statement each. The stipulation nuance stays in stop condition 1 and the BCI/CJDISS sentence stays in the proposed order and the counsel flags.

defectsFoundAndResolved.found: The shared renderer's default requested-relief clause (b) and default order paragraph direct every criminal justice agency holding the record to act, which exceeds what Chapter 12-60.1 grants.
defectsFoundAndResolved.resolution: The configuration supplies exact clauses through the two optional presentation fields requested in CAPTAIN_PATCH_REQUEST_SHARED_RENDERER.md. Byte preservation for every other configuration is proven by scripts/verify-nd-shared-renderer-byte-preservation.mjs, and the absence of the default text is asserted by test.

acceptedLimitations.limitation: The proof of service certifies service of 'this Petition'. The proposed order is served with it, and the note above the certification says so, but the certification line itself names only the petition because the shared renderer builds it from the configuration's filing noun.
acceptedLimitations.whyAccepted: Fixing the certification line would need a second, larger change to a shared renderer this lane does not own, for a document whose adjacent sentence already states the full scope of what was served. Recorded rather than widened.
